evals.prompt: I want to release the kan workspace to crates.io. It has three crates: kan-core, kan-adapters (depends on kan-core), and kan-cli (depends on both). Walk me through a dry run first, then the real release.
evals.expected_output: Runs the orchestrate.py script in --dry-run mode on /Users/joe/dev/kan, shows the publish order (kan-core → kan-adapters → kan-cli), runs quality gates, then confirms with user before offering the real run command.

assertions.text: Script invoked with --dry-run flag before any real publish
Publish order is kan-core before kan-adapters before kan-cli
User asked to confirm before real publish is initiated
Real run command is shown after dry-run completes

evals.prompt: My kan workspace release got interrupted after kan-core published but before kan-adapters. How do I resume without re-publishing kan-core?
evals.expected_output: Instructs user to re-run with --resume flag; explains .release-state.json tracks published crates; kan-core will be skipped (skipped status), kan-adapters and kan-cli will proceed.

assertions.text: Confirms kan-core will be skipped, not re-published

evals.prompt: The clippy gate keeps failing on kan-adapters even after auto-fix. I've manually fixed it now. How do I continue the release without running the full gate suite again?
evals.expected_output: Explains --skip-gates flag; may also mention --resume if a partial run was already in progress; provides the exact command to continue from where they left off.

assertions.text: Provides a complete command the user can run immediately
Does not suggest re-running fmt or clippy manually
